readout_other: fMRI tSNR in left/right M1 during passive and active sonication; targeting off-target distance on T1w; post-session symptom questionnaire
direction_notes: Methods and workflow paper; the authors state it does not present TUS stimulation results or evaluate neuromodulatory effects. The outcome was MRI signal quality (tSNR) and targeting accuracy.
safety_notes: No participants reported adverse events and no sessions were terminated; post-session symptom questionnaire administered to 16 cap participants (headache 4/16 most common); simulations constrained to MI < 1.9 and temperature rise < 2 C.

source_quotes.n_subjects: To assess whether active sonication introduced electromagnetic interference (EMI)-related signal degradation beyond that observed with the passive transducer, fMRI tSNR was evaluated in left and right M1 ROIs across 12 participants (Subjects 6-17) under both passive transducer and active sonication conditions.
